open_points.subject: Operation-node NodeExecution ownership (`effects` vs `runs`)
open_points.text: `effects` owns "then one store call writes the outcome: the EffectAttempt's conclusion, the next NodeExecution..."; `runs` owns "A12–A15: ... the trace and its order".
open_points.question: Which module is the single owner of writing and ordering NodeExecution records for operation nodes?
options: `effects` writes operation-node NodeExecution records (and `runs` only writes function/skip/upstream records)
`runs` writes all NodeExecution records (and `effects` returns outcome data only)
open_points.default_guess: `effects` writes operation-node NodeExecution records because A11 rule 1 couples them transactionally with EffectAttempt updates.

open_points.subject: Disclosure-class order source of truth (`data_provider` vs `canonical_values`)
open_points.text: `data_provider` owns "the ordered disclosure classes of A07 rule 1"; `canonical_values` owns "The order of disclosure classes and the highest class of a set".
open_points.question: Which module is authoritative for class ordering semantics so all comparisons use one source?
options: `data_provider` is source-of-truth constants; `canonical_values` must only consume them
`canonical_values` defines and owns the ordering internally, and `data_provider` is informational
open_points.default_guess: Treat `data_provider` constants as authoritative and make `canonical_values` a pure consumer.

open_points.subject: State 2 decision A21 (security review gate)
open_points.text: State 3 says it is "Derived from the accepted State 2 decisions A01–A21", but no module section names ownership of A21 (`design_lint --state 2` complete review record, reference resolution).
open_points.question: Is A21 implemented by any kernel module, or explicitly outside runtime modules as a process/tooling obligation?
options: Own A21 in a non-runtime tooling module outside this module stack
Assign A21 ownership to an existing module (e.g., `surface`)
Declare A21 out of code scope for later states
open_points.default_guess: Treat A21 as external tooling/process, not runtime module code.

open_points.subject: Atomic boundary for send outcome vs run state updates
open_points.text: `effects` hides "the two store calls around every send" and "must not own ... what a run's status is"; `runs` owns waiting points and run status.
open_points.question: When an operation attempt concludes, are run/waiting-state changes required in the same transaction as EffectAttempt+NodeExecution writes, and which module performs that write?
options: `effects` transaction also updates run waiting/status via store call contracts defined for `runs`
`effects` commits attempt+NodeExecution only; `runs` updates run state in a following transaction
open_points.default_guess: Keep A11-coupled records in `effects` transaction and let `runs` derive/update run status immediately after in a separate call unless explicitly required atomic.
